solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A child's horse is into his food

indicators.note: the word into tells us one piece goes inside the other, here inside the word his

parts.note: taken as written
gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse, shortened to GG

explanation.surface: A boy's toy horse has got into his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: GG (gee-gee) is a child's word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a Scottish dish of offal and oatmeal, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Answer on edge — "I'm here"

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone answering from the brink announces their presence.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cough to draw attention, the polite noise for announcing you are present.

clue.text: Sponsor daughter and gross husband to stop one after the other

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so these pieces fill the gap inside the other word

parts.note: a goer is someone eager for, or chasing after, the opposite sex
gross can mean fat or obese

explanation.surface: Someone sponsoring a family, with a daughter and overweight husband, halts things in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One after the other' reads as 'in turn' but stands for a goer, a person chasing the other sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Forge title of Cambridge University in short

indicators.note: the word in places the university's initials within the word for short

parts.note: shy can mean short of, as in two pounds shy of the total
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is a university in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Someone fakes the name of Cambridge University for brevity.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge here is the one in Massachusetts, not England.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's workshop, where metal is heated and hammered, is called a forge.

clue.text: Cornmeal needing space to grow

parts.note: mush is American porridge made from cornmeal
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Cornmeal needs space to grow, like dough rising.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this means to expand rapidly, the way fungi spring up overnight.

clue.text: Moderate drivers may go over it

definitions.meaning: describes views that are neither extreme left nor right
motorists cross the central line of a highway when overtaking

explanation.surface: A moderate stance, and a line drivers cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrist position is described with the phrase for the centre of a highway.

clue.text: School set to host extremely louche old poet from Germany

indicators.note: a host takes someone in, so the outer pieces hold the louche letters

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of louche

explanation.surface: A school is preparing to welcome a very disreputable German poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to host' puts LE, the outer letters of louche, into SCH plus GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: August Wilhelm Schlegel was a German Romantic poet and translator of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Pass right over topless bathing area?

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece written over another sits above it
topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a beach is where people bathe in the sea

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion to pass by a nudist beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes B from BEACH, leaving EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something to someone is to stretch out and hand it over, as reaching does.

clue.text: Dry article on sportsman's partner in back numbers

indicators.note: in places the article and partner inside the reversed numbers
back says the abbreviations for numbers are read the other way

parts.note: No. is short for number, so two numbers give NO NO

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: the is the definite article
a WAG is a wife or girlfriend of a footballer

explanation.surface: A dry article about a footballer's girlfriend, appearing in back issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NONO into ONON; WAGs are the wives and girlfriends of England footballers, a British tabloid term.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry means abstaining from alcohol, which the idiom describes.

clue.text: Bluster by chief opposition to progress?

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is put beside the other

parts.note: head means chief, as in head of department
wind is empty talk or bluster

explanation.surface: A boss's blustering talk is a barrier to getting anything done.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale blowing against you holds back forward movement, literally opposing progress.

clue.text: Make out tinny, hollow sound

parts.note: to make out a noise is to hear it

indicators.note: hollow means the inside is emptied, leaving the outer letters of tinny

explanation.surface: Detect a thin, empty noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of healthy and robust, as in sound in body.

clue.text: Shivering in water around bank is a sign of weakness

indicators.note: in tells us the shivering word goes inside the water word
around here turns the water word back to front

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a chill is a feverish shivering
to heel is to lean over, as a ship or aircraft banks

explanation.surface: Shivering in cold water near a riverbank shows frailty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses the water word; 'bank' is the verb used of a tilting aircraft or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Greek hero vulnerable only at his heel, the phrase means a fatal flaw.

clue.text: Somehow Elgar repeatedly exposed antiphony in work by G&S, say

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters are arranged in some unspecified new way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: exposed strips the outer layer; doing it twice peels two letters from each end of antiphony

explanation.surface: Elgar's call-and-response piece somehow exposed in a Gilbert and Sullivan show.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping antiphony's ends twice leaves TIPHO, mixed with ELGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's Savoy operas are the classic examples of the comic operetta genre.

clue.text: Reportedly look for religious disciple

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that is heard like the synonym

parts.note: to seek is to look for

explanation.surface: Apparently someone is searching for a devout follower.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the faith founded by Guru Nanak comes from a Punjabi word for disciple or learner.

clue.text: Pick up deliveries in the arena, centrally

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler

indicators.note: centrally means only the central stretch of the words the arena is kept, its ends dropped

explanation.surface: A fielder catching balls bowled in the middle of a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' trims T from the front and ENA from the back of THE ARENA, leaving HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a conversation is to catch it by chance, listening without being meant to.

clue.text: Digitally gain access to lift

parts.note: sounds like hacking, but means using a thumb, a digit, to get a ride from passing drivers

explanation.surface: Sounds like hacking into an elevator's computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by thumbing rides is done with a raised digit to obtain a lift in a car.

clue.text: Dog briefly plodding in London borough

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word to be cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a hound is a dog
plodding means moving slowly

explanation.surface: A dog ambling for a while through a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hounslow is a borough in west London, home to Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the 32 boroughs of Greater London, in the west of the city.

clue.text: Distribution of Thoreau's novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of Thoreau with the s

explanation.surface: How Thoreau's book was sold around.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividing up of something among people is an allocation or distribution.

clue.text: A very small measure of you in a previous life?

definitions.meaning: a thousandth of an inch, a mil
the archaic form of you, used in earlier centuries

explanation.surface: A tiny unit, and a reincarnation riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny engineering unit, and the second-person pronoun of old English.

clue.text: Left long after gremlin initiated bug

indicators.note: after says the left and long pieces follow the gremlin letter
initiated points to the starting letter of gremlin

parts.note: to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A gremlin started a bug after the left side was left long.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault or hitch in a system, the same as a computer bug.

clue.text: Vulgar riches displayed by body politic

parts.note: common can mean vulgar or low-class
wealth means riches

explanation.surface: A nation flaunting its crass affluence.
explanation.definitionFit: A state or community of people governed together, a political body.

clue.text: Miniature tool cutter initially made hole incorrectly

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of made
incorrectly says the letters of hole are set in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny cutting device first drilled a hole badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tool' is a cheeky word for the penis, which is why it is miniature on an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish official trained to perform circumcision on baby boys.

clue.text: Maybe Oxford scholar's opening theorem regularly scanned

indicators.note: opening points to the first letter of scholar's
reading theorem at regular intervals takes every second letter

explanation.surface: An Oxford student's opening theorem, routinely studied.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford here is a laced leather style of footwear, not the university.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a style of lace-up footwear, so it is an example of the item.

clue.text: Bishop marrying girl in jolly place of worship

indicators.note: marrying joins the two pieces together side by side

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Ethel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bishop wedding a girl at a cheerful chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: A jolly is slang for a Royal Marine; a bethel is often a chapel for seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bethel is a nonconformist chapel, or one for sailors: a house of God.

clue.text: Maths subject on open-access course wanting head teachers to start at once

indicators.note: on means one piece is placed beside the other

parts.note: OU is the Open University, open to all without entry qualifications
trig is short for trigonometry
H is the standard abbreviation for head

indicators.note: to start points to the first letter of teachers

explanation.surface: An Open University maths course needs head teachers to begin immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright as an adverb means immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Revered passage submitted without introduction

parts.note: a hall is an entrance passage

indicators.note: without introduction removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: bowed means submitted, as in bowed to pressure

explanation.surface: A respected corridor yielded with no preamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without introduction' removes B from BOWED, leaving OWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means holy or deeply honoured, as in hallowed ground.

clue.text: Dog's disc, not wide, about to be returned

indicators.note: not wide drops the cricket abbreviation W for a wide

parts.note: a wheel is a disc shape

indicators.note: returned says the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A dog's frisbee, thrown short, about to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeler is a cattle dog, such as the Australian breed that nips at heels.
